Questions

Copilot adoption, a system launch, course libraries, and whether the training changed the work.

Is this only about AI?

A new ERP, CRM or HR system needs the same thing as Copilot: people who can do their real work with it. I build the learning, change and practice layer around the system you are launching.

System launch

Do you build AI models or chatbots?

I build Copilot agents in your existing Microsoft 365 setup, and small assistants on top of tools you already run, such as the assistant on this site. Then I train people to use them. I don't train ML models, and your IT team owns the deep integration.

Is it safe to use AI on our content?

We agree in writing what data any tool may use before anything is built. If a document shouldn't go into a tool, it doesn't. Hidden, unofficial use is often riskier than a setup with clear rules.

AI licences

What's the difference between Copilot training and a Copilot agent in daily work?

Training shows people what the tool can do. An agent carries one team's actual workflow, inside the Microsoft 365 you already run, so people practise on their own tasks. Most organisations have run the training without the agent, and usage stalls after the course.

AI licences

Our people have had the AI training. How do you get them to use it?

I start with one team, a handful of real tasks, and their manager in the room. We build or tune a Copilot agent for that workflow, practise on the work they already do, and keep only what they use. BCG's 2025 research (opens in a new tab) is blunt about this: people with clear leadership support use AI regularly at twice the rate of those without it.

Can you show that training changed the work, not just completions?

I can if we agree, before we start, what should change and how you will see it. That is usually usage plus one or two measures from the work itself. On CBRE's myBuy training I used a show me, try me, test me design so the check was part of the course. I won't invent a return-on-investment figure I can't back.

Training impact

We're launching SAP, Dynamics or Workday. What do you do before go-live?

People practise the tasks that change for their role, in a safe copy of the system, and they have a short guide when they get stuck. I also look at the learning platform that will carry the training, so it works for learners and for admins. Practice before go-live matters even more when people are already tired of change.

System launch

How do you capture knowledge that's stuck in a few experts' heads?

We capture it once, in a form people can learn from and look up. Repeat questions go to a guide or an assistant first. Experts see only the hard ones. I've done this as a knowledge map and trainee path for Clarksons, and as a Loop knowledge hub with an AI assistant in an in-house role, which participants voted to keep.

Expert knowledge

Do you replace our LMS, or work with what we already run?

I work with what you already run unless it clearly can't do the job. I have shipped work in Storyline, Rise, Open edX, Moodle and Drupal. In 2019 I advised Advanced Learning Company against a long build from scratch; their Open edX platform, Advanced Learning World, went live in 3.5 months once delivery started.

Course library

What happens when you leave? Can our team run this?

The work is finished when your team can run it without me. That means documentation, a working handover, and practice for the people who will own it. On SITCIN, 2025 to 2026, the original developer had left no admin guide, so I wrote one, handed the git repository to UNECE IT, and worked through the deployment blockers with them.

How I work

Do you work with UN agencies and public bodies?

Yes. I have long-term work with UNECE, including SITCIN in 2025 to 2026, and with OSCE, including the eTIR guidance site and explainer video. International programmes usually need one framework that still works in more than one language and more than one country.

Where do you work, and who can you work with?

I am eligible to work in the EU, the UK and Australia. I work remotely, or on site by arrangement. I normally reply within two working days.

Contact

How long does a typical engagement take?

It depends on the scope, which I write down before we start. Some work is one team and one workflow. Some is a course library or a platform that has to go through a pilot first. You can start small. If the brief is a fit, I will tell you what the work involves in that conversation.

How I work

Do you also refresh e-learning and course libraries?

Yes. I help you decide which courses to keep, fix, convert, rebuild or retire, and I update only the packages whose content has changed. I also built a SCORM Package Editor so you can open a package in the browser, edit it and export it, without uploading the files to me.

Course library

Will you use our project as a public case study?

Only if you agree, and only in wording you have seen. Some proof I already use is written so the employer is not named. I don't invent results, and I don't publish figures we didn't measure.
